mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is continuous and negative: each 10bps decrease in FEDFUNDS predicts a 0.1% increase in 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no positive correlation with FEDFUNDS level (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window, or the relationship reverses (negative slope) in the walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 245.0 signals an inflationary environment that forces central banks to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods where CPIAUCSL > 245.0 are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is activated when both series rise by more than 0.1% and 0.2% respectively in the past month.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% in 1 month AND CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise by the specified thresholds are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, defined by unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% and monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5%, signals robust economic conditions that support positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 AND PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in periods meeting the strong labor market condition are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market recovery, indicated by housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1220.0, signals improving consumer confidence and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in periods where HOUST > 1220.0 are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A robust industrial production level (INDPRO) above 105.0 indicates strong manufacturing activity, supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in periods where INDPRO > 105.0 are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a strong housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is activated when both series rise by more than 0.5% in the past month.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 0.5% in 1 month AND HOUST growth > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods where both RSAFS and HOUST rise by the specified thresholds are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of residential sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The relationship is continuous and positive: each 1% increase in RSAFS predicts a 0.05% increase in 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no positive correlation with RSAFS level (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window, or the relationship reverses (negative slope) in the walk-forward test.
